places.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
places.about: This is Seoul's grandest Joseon Dynasty-era palace and the seat of power for centuries before it was razed in 1592 by a Japanese invasion (and again by the Japanese in 1910).
places.tip: Main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty.
places.looks: A large walled palace at the foot of a rocky, cone-shaped mountain (Bugaksan). From outside you see a long pale stone wall with a gate tower in front, and behind it many halls with dark grey tiled roofs.

closed.text: Closed on Tuesdays. When a public holiday or a substitute holiday falls on the regular closing day, open; closed the day after the holiday instead.

source.name: Korea Heritage Service, Royal Palaces and Tombs Center (official)

events.name: Free guided tour (English)
events.note: Starts in front of Gyeongbokgung Palace Information Center inside Heungnyemun Gate; about 1 to 1.5 hours; groups of 10+ reserve in advance

price.text: Adults (age 19-64) 3,000 won individual, 2,400 won group (10+). Free: aged 18 and below, seniors 65+, those wearing a Hanbok, Culture Day (last Wednesday of every month). Royal Palace Pass covers 4 palaces and Jongmyo Shrine within three months.

places.transit: Gyeongbokgung (Metro Line 3) or Gwanghwamun stn (Metro Line 5, across the Gwanghwamun plaza)

places.name: Gwanghwamun Gate
places.about: Main gate of Geongbokgung Palace (also known as Kyŏngbokkung Palace).
places.tip: Main (south) gate of Gyeongbokgung; the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony is held here.
places.looks: A two-tiered wooden gate tower with grey tiled roofs and painted eaves, sitting on a long pale stone base pierced by three arched openings. A wide raised stone terrace with low stone railings stretches out in front of it, and stone walls run off to both sides.

events.name: Changing of the Royal Palace Guard Ceremony
About these times
events.note: This is the February 2026 notice, the latest schedule notice found on the official board. Ceremonial events can be cancelled due to weather (rain, heat wave; e.g. suspended 2026-08-05 for a heat-wave warning, resumed 2026-08-08). The notice does not say whether the ceremony runs on Tuesdays.

places.name: Heungnyemun Gate
places.about: Second gate of the Korean royal palace.
places.tip: Second gate inside Gwanghwamun. Official site: free tours start at the Information Center inside Heungnyemun.
places.looks: Inside Gwanghwamun, across a wide sandy courtyard, stands a second gate with a two-tiered roof, joined on both sides by long single-storey corridors with red pillars.

closed.text: Closed on Tuesdays. When a public holiday or a substitute holiday falls on the regular closing day, open; closed the day after the holiday instead.

places.name: Geunjeongjeon Hall
places.about: Hall in Gyeongbokgung, Seoul, South Korea.
places.looks: The largest hall: two storeys of deep painted eaves under grey tiled roofs, set on a two-level stone platform with carved stone railings and central stairs. A wide courtyard paved with rough stone slabs lies in front, with mountains behind.

closed.text: Closed on Tuesdays. When a public holiday or a substitute holiday falls on the regular closing day, open; closed the day after the holiday instead.

places.name: Gyeonghoeru Pavilion
places.about: Royal Banquet Hall.
places.looks: A very large open pavilion raised on rows of stone pillars, standing in a square pond. Its long grey tiled roof is reflected in the water, and small islands with pine trees sit beside it.

closed.text: Closed on Tuesdays. When a public holiday or a substitute holiday falls on the regular closing day, open; closed the day after the holiday instead.

places.name: Hyangwonjeong Pavilion
places.about: Pavilion of Gyeongbokgung Palace.
places.looks: A small, slender two-storey pavilion with six sides and a pointed tiled roof, standing on a grassy island in a pond. The rocky peak of Bugaksan rises behind it.

closed.text: Closed on Tuesdays. When a public holiday or a substitute holiday falls on the regular closing day, open; closed the day after the holiday instead.

places.name: Dongsipjagak
places.looks: A small square watchtower with a tiled pavilion roof on top of a tall block of cut stone. It stands alone at a road junction, with cars passing and modern glass towers behind it.

places.name: National Palace Museum of Korea
places.about: National museum.
places.looks: A long, low modern building with a traditional-style tiled roof edge, reached by a broad flight of stone steps. The name '국립고궁박물관 / National Palace Museum of Korea' is on a dark board above the glass entrance.

closed.text: January 1st; February 17th (Seollal); September 25th (Chuseok); the last Monday of every month (if that is a public holiday, closed the following day).

hours.conflict: Wikivoyage hours (10:00-18:00, Wed/Sat to 21:00) differ from the official page (09:30-17:30, Sat to 21:30).

events.name: Guided tours for international visitors (English, Japanese, Chinese)
events.when: Weekdays (Mon-Fri) 13:00-15:00; meeting point Information Desk, 2nd floor lobby; monthly language calendar on the page

places.name: National Folk Museum of Korea
places.about: National museum in Seoul, South Korea.
places.looks: A tall five-tiered pagoda-shaped tower rises above a white stone building with wide twin stairways. It stands at the north-east side of the palace grounds, with a large open forecourt in front.

closed.text: January 1st; Seollal (Lunar New Year's Day); July 7 (Tue) 2026 temporary closure; Chuseok.

hours.conflict: Wikivoyage hours (09:00-17:00) are only the winter hours on the official page (Mar-Oct 09:00-18:00).

events.name: English docent tour
events.note: Meeting place: information desk, 1st floor lobby; free; foreign visitors only

price.text: Free (all exhibitions). Note: the museum is inside the Gyeongbokgung grounds; the page says Gyeongbokgung admission is charged and bought at the Gyeongbokgung ticket office.

places.name: Gwanghwamun Square
places.about: A center of Seoul. The name came from the main gate of the Gyeongbokgung. The site was a location of the Six Ministries during the Joseon dynasty and was a large motorway since then.
places.looks: A wide paved square beside the main road, Sejong-daero, with planted beds, umbrellas and large statues. At its north end, across a road crossing, you look straight at Gwanghwamun Gate with mountains behind.
places.transit: Line 5, Gwanghwamun Station; Exit 9 directly leads to the plaza

places.name: Statue of King Sejong the Great
places.about: Monument in Seoul, South Korea.
places.looks: A large golden-bronze statue of a seated king on a throne, one hand raised, holding an open book in the other. It sits on a stone plinth carved with '세종대왕' (King Sejong the Great) in Korean letters.

places.name: Statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin
places.about: Statue in Seoul.
places.looks: A dark bronze statue of an armoured admiral holding a long sword, standing on a tall stone pillar at the south end of the square. Looking north past it you can see the mountains and the palace gate in the distance.

places.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
places.about: Since its independence from Japan, Korea has experienced a series of political events during a short period. You can see exhibitions that show war, dictatorships, uprisings against dictatorships, and industrialization that happened in South Korea.
places.looks: A wide, flat-fronted modern building in pale grey with long horizontal bands, facing Sejong-daero, with a flagpole and lawn in front. The museum name is on the upper part of the facade.

closed.text: Page text: 'The Museum is closed on January 1, New Year's Day, Chuseok.' (New Year's Day here likely means Seollal, the Lunar New Year; not stated)

source.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History (official)

src: https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Seoul/Jongno&oldid=5433820 (listing 'National Museum of Korean Contemporary History', line 156)

places.name: MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art)
places.about: MMCA Seoul opened in 2013. The site had been the Korean Armed Forces Capital Hospital and the Defense Security Command.
places.looks: A three-storey red-brick building with rows of large steel-framed windows and a white entrance canopy carrying the museum name in Korean and English. Low steps lead up from the street.

closed.text: Jan. 1, Lunar New Year's day, and Chuseok

hours.conflict: Wikivoyage price '₩4,000'; the official page says paid exhibition fees vary (All Pass 10,000 KRW).

price.text: Paid exhibition tickets: fees vary by exhibition. All Pass Ticket 10,000 KRW (when 3 or more paid exhibitions run). Free on Wed and Sat late opening (18:00-21:00) and on Culture Day (last Wednesday of every month). Free for individuals under 24 or over 65, undergraduate students and some card holders (ID required).

places.transit: 14 minute walk from Exit No. 1 from Ankuk Station. 17-minute walk from Exit No. 2 from Gwanghwamun Station. Right across the east gate of Gyeongbok Palace.
src: https://en.wikivoyage.org/w/index.php?title=Seoul/Jongno&oldid=5433820 (listing 'MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea)', line 165)

places.name: Samcheong-ro (Samcheong-dong street)
places.about: Road in Seoul, South Korea.
places.tip: Street of cafes, galleries and shops north-east of Gyeongbokgung.
places.looks: A gently sloping street with cafes and small shops lined up on top of a stone retaining wall, some with umbrellas on roof terraces. A row of trees and a low railing run along the pavement.

places.name: Jeongdok Library
places.about: Public library in Seoul.
places.tip: Public library (Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education).
places.looks: A three-storey pale yellow building in an old school style with a central arched doorway, behind a garden with pine trees. A round fountain basin with a white bowl-shaped centrepiece sits in front of it.

places.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
places.about: The collective name of the few tiny suburbs ("dong") wedged between Gyeongbuk Palace and the Secret Garden, just north of Insadong and Anguk Station.
places.looks: Steep, narrow paved lanes lined with hanok houses: grey curved tiled roofs, wooden gates and patterned stone walls. From the upper lanes you can look down over the roofs to downtown high-rises and a tower on a hill (N Seoul Tower).

closed.text: Tourist visits prohibited 17:00 - 10:00 next day in the Red Zone (about 34,000 m2 around Bukchon-ro 11-gil).

hours.note: Tourists may visit the Red Zone only 10:00-17:00. From 17:00 to 10:00 next day, tourist visits are prohibited.

price.text: No admission (public residential streets). Fine for violation: 100,000 won (enforced from 2025-03-01; guidance period 2024-11-01 to 2025-02-28).

places.transit: get off at Exit 2 of Anguk Station and walk along the road for about 10 minutes to get there

places.name: Bukchon 5th Scenic Spot: Gahoe-dong Alley
places.looks: A narrow lane between old walls of stone and brick, with hanok roofs on the right and trees hanging over the walls; the lane slopes down and bends out of sight.

closed.text: Tourist visits prohibited 17:00 - 10:00 next day in the Red Zone (about 34,000 m2 around Bukchon-ro 11-gil).

hours.note: Tourists may visit the Red Zone only 10:00-17:00. From 17:00 to 10:00 next day, tourist visits are prohibited.

price.text: No admission (public residential streets). Fine for violation: 100,000 won (enforced from 2025-03-01; guidance period 2024-11-01 to 2025-02-28).

places.name: Bukchon Observatory
places.about: Provides a sweeping view of Bukchon Village and the greater Seoul cityscape, with Lotte Tower and the palace both clearly visible.
places.looks: According to Wikivoyage it is a converted apartment with a rooftop view, 'tucked away' and easy to miss; from the top you can see over Bukchon to the palace and the city. (No photo.)

places.name: Baek In-je House
places.about: Building in Jongno District, South Korea.
places.looks: A tall traditional gate with its own small tiled roof, at the top of a wide flight of stone steps. Long white-plastered walls with grey tiled tops run to both sides, with a garden of shrubs and rocks below.

closed.text: January 1; every Monday (open if Monday is a public holiday).

source.name: Seoul Museum of History (official, Korean page)

events.name: Foreign-language guided tour
events.when: 16:00 - Wednesday Japanese, Thursday Chinese, Friday English (booking or on-site sign-up)

places.name: Seoul Museum of Craft Art
places.about: The Seoul Craft Museum can experience the technical, practical, artistic, and cultural values of crafts by studying and sharing not only crafts but also knowledge, records, people, and the environment surrounding crafts.
places.tip: Official English name 'Seoul Museum of Craft Art (SeMoCA)'.
places.looks: A long, low pale building with rows of identical windows and a modern glass-walled wing, around a wide open lawn and courtyard.

hours.conflict: OSM opening_hours 'Mo-Su 10:00-18:00' says open on Mondays; the official page says closed every Monday.

places.name: Unhyeongung
places.about: A museum in the former palace of a Joseon Dynasty archduke Heungseon, who was the father of the second last king of Joseon. It has several mannequins depicting the costumes of the yangban or noble class during the Joseon Dynasty.
places.looks: Inside the walls: a single-storey hanok hall on a high stone platform, with dark wooden pillars, white paper-panel doors and a grey tiled roof. Hanging boards with writing are fixed to the pillars.

closed.text: Closed every Monday (open if Monday is a public holiday).

places.name: Donhwamun Gate (Changdeokgung Palace)
places.about: The main gate of Changdeokgung Palace.
places.tip: Main gate of Changdeokgung, at the east edge of the area.
places.looks: A large two-storey wooden gate with red pillars, painted eaves and a double tiled roof, set back from the road behind a low railing and a small open plaza. Its name board reads 敦化門.

closed.text: Closed on Mondays. When a public holiday or substitute holiday falls on the closing day, open; closed the day after instead.

source.name: Korea Heritage Service, Royal Palaces and Tombs Center (official)

hours.note: Secret Garden (separate ticket area): March - June / September - October 10:00-17:30; July - August 10:00-17:10; November 10:00-17:00; December - February 10:00-16:10.

price.text: Palace Building Area: adult (19-64) 3,000 won (group 2,400). Free: 18 and under, over 65, those wearing Hanbok, Culture Day (last Wednesday of every month). Secret Garden: adult 5,000 won plus general admission; senior 5,000; youth (7-18) 2,500; limited to 100 people per session (50 online, 50 on site); entry only at the ticket time. Royal Palace Pass 6,000 won (4 palaces & Jongmyo, excluding Secret Garden).

places.name: Jogyesa Temple
places.about: The chief temple of the Jogye order of Buddhism, the dominant branch of Buddhism in Korea. As such, it is one of the most important modern Buddhist temples in the country.
places.looks: A big temple hall with richly painted green, red and blue woodwork and a steep tiled roof, with a red gable carrying a gold three-circle emblem. A large old tree with pale bark stands in the courtyard in front, next to a white stone statue.

hours.note: The official English pages (index, Access) give no visiting hours.

places.name: Insa-dong Street (Insadong-gil)
places.about: Insadong is an area known for its art galleries and shops and is possibly the most touristy place in South Korea. It is a great place to buy cultural souvenirs. There are also a few stores that offer interesting vintage toys and various kitsch.
places.looks: A long street lined with tall trees, low shop buildings and small signs, wide enough for walkers to use the middle. Benches and planters sit along the edges.

places.name: Ssamziegil
places.about: Ssamziegil is a shopping complex that opened in 2004.
places.looks: A four-storey building built around an open courtyard, with a walkway that ramps up around the yard past rows of small shops with glass fronts.

places.name: Museum Kimchikan
places.about: A museum (previously known as Kimchi Field Museum) about all things kimchi. Includes a lot of interactive exhibits and comes with a free audio guide in English. There are also hands-on kimchi-making programs, only on reservation, however.

closed.text: Every Monday; January 1; 3 days of Seollal and Chuseok holidays; December 25

events.name: Audio guide (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)
events.when: Any time; free; scan QR code with own phone, bring earphones

price.text: Individual: adult 5,000 won, student 3,000 won, preschool child 2,000 won. Groups 20+: 4,000 / 2,000 / 1,000 won. Free: infants under 36 months, seniors 65+, people with disabilities and their companion (ID required).

places.transit: Subway line 3, Anguk Station, 10 minutes walk along Insadong-gil

places.name: Tapgol Park
places.about: A small park frequented by the elderly and the footsore traveler. Contains a 500-year-old namesake pagoda under protective glass and a nice large gazebo to get out of the sun.
places.looks: The park entrance is a wide traditional gate with green-painted woodwork, red pillars and a tiled roof, with a sign board reading '삼일문'. Inside is a paved yard with an eight-sided pavilion under a tiled roof.

hours.note: Opening hours could not be confirmed from an official source.

places.transit: you can arrive at Jonggak Station Exit 3-2 and go straight

places.name: Cheondogyo Central Temple
places.about: Building in Jongno District, South Korea.
places.looks: A red-brick building with white stone trim, a tall central tower topped by a small dome and spire, and a round window near the top of the tower. An arched doorway is at the foot of the tower.

places.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village
places.about: Neighbourhood in Seoul, South Korea.
places.looks: A maze of very narrow paved alleys between low hanok with tiled roofs, now mostly cafes and small shops with painted doors and small signs. From above it is a dense patch of grey roofs surrounded by taller buildings.

places.name: Imun Seolleongtang
places.about: The oldest extant restaurant in South Korea, founded around 1904. Serves seolleongtang (beef stew).

places.name: Sadong Myeonok
places.about: Justly famous for its manduguk, a soup of gargantuan homemade dumplings stuffed with meat and veggies and served with side dishes for ₩5,000. English menu available.

places.name: Gaesong Mandu Koong
places.about: Specialty restaurant for mandu (Korean dumplings) from the nearby Kaesong region in North Korea. The chickpea patties are also very good. This restaurant has been passed down from mother to daughter for three generations.
places.transit: take insa-dong 10-gil from the main street insa-dong gil and then it is about 15 meters on the left

places.name: Samcheongdong Sujebi
places.about: Canteen style ambiance, renowned for serving good Sujaebi - a mild soup where the noodles are flattened and torn into sheets. Always packed with people so be prepared for a queue.

places.name: Uyeonhwa
places.about: The Hanok-style restaurant in Ikseon-dong blends modern sensibilities and traditional atmosphere. It features Hamburg steak made with 100 percent Korean beef and is served with hot pot rice.

places.name: Sinrajemyeon (Anguk)
places.about: It is a kalguksu specialty store that originated in Gyeongju, and is located in Anguk Station in Seoul. It features a traditional Korean interior with a luxurious atmosphere.

places.name: Chwiyabeol Guksi
places.about: Dumpling hot pot is a particularly famous noodle restaurant. Dumpling hot pot here boasts a deep and cool taste of soup with a combination of large dumplings and fresh vegetables.

places.name: Eomyongbaek Dwaeji Gukbap
places.about: It is a restaurant that serves Busan style pork and rice soup in a tranquil hanok atmosphere. The main menu here is pork and rice soup in two styles, clear and thick, and kimchi and kkakdugi, served as basic side dishes, go well with gukbap.

places.name: Gwanghwamun Mijin
places.about: As a traditional buckwheat specialty, cold buckwheat noodles and handmade pork cutlet are the main dishes. The restaurant is spacious and quick-rotating, and the Yeolmu Kimchi and pickled radish served as standard side dishes are delicious.

hours.conflict: OSM opening_hours (Mo-Su 10:00-22:00) and Wikivoyage hours (10:30-21:00) differ.

places.name: Artist Bakery
places.about: It is a bakery specializing in various kinds of salt bread, featuring a savory and salty taste.

places.name: Tteoksang
places.about: This restaurant offers a fusion of Korean tteokbokki (rice cakes) in a hanok charming setting.

places.name: Pungnyeon Ssal Nongsan
places.about: cheap snack places. noodle sausage, fried stuff, fried rice cake...

places.name: Ikseon-dong Meat Restaurant
places.about: Korean barbecue in a hanok with exposed wooden rafters, where staff grill the meat at your table. Korean pork cuts such as minari samgyeopsal, galmaegisal and kkotmoksal, plus wagyu sirloin and kimchi jjigae. Group seating and outdoor tables in the alley.

price.text: ₩18,000 per 180 g serving, pork set for two ₩54,000

places.transit: 2 min walk from exit 6 of Jongno 3-ga station

places.name: Gyeongbokgung Station Exit 5
places.tip: Line 3. Exit on the palace side.

places.name: Anguk Station Exit 1
places.tip: Line 3. Seoul Museum of Craft Art is 50 m from Exit 1 (official museum page).

places.name: Anguk Station Exit 6
places.tip: Line 3. Toward Insa-dong and Jogyesa (Jogyesa official page: Exit 6).

places.name: Jongno 3-ga Station Exit 5
places.tip: Lines 1/3/5. Toward Ikseon-dong and Tapgol Park.

notes.text: In the Bukchon Red Zone (the hanok lanes around Bukchon-ro 11-gil) tourists may visit only from 10:00 to 17:00; from 17:00 to 10:00 the next day tourist visits are not allowed.
Insa-dong is a vehicle-free zone on Saturday afternoons and Sundays (as stated on the Jogyesa official page).
